date_note: Remarks made at FedTalks on the day CyberScoop published; the page gives no earlier day.
exec: GSA says quantum-resistant credentials can be built on PIV cards in use today, and that testing for bugs and interoperability must continue.
plain: A US government agency says it put new quantum-resistant security code directly on the chip of ID smart cards used today and issued new credentials with it. It says more testing is still needed.
summary: At FedTalks, GSA's Dan Pomeroy said technologists loaded new post-quantum algorithms directly onto the chip of smart PIV cards and issued new credentials. Pomeroy said the work showed quantum-resistant credentials are "achievable with the cards we have today" and that the government must keep testing for bugs and interoperability issues. CyberScoop did not name the algorithms used.
title: GSA says it ran post-quantum algorithms on existing PIV smart cards
